target_customer: Wind farm owners and operators and turbine OEMs that pay for blade and tower inspection, cleaning, coating and repair
problem: Wind turbine blades need frequent inspection, cleaning and repair, which is done by rope technicians working at height at high cost and risk, with long turbine downtime.
business_model: Robot-enabled maintenance and inspection services sold to operators and OEMs, with inspection data delivered through a customer portal
product_category: Robotics services for wind turbine maintenance

founders.name: Dainis Kruze
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CEO on the YC page and the Aerones about page. Background not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Janis Putrams
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CTO on the Aerones about page. Education and prior employers not found in opened sources.

competitors.name: Rope Robotics
competitors.what: Danish developer of a robot for wind turbine blade leading edge repair
competitors.funding_then: EUR 2 million Danish government support announced December 2018

technical_complexity.rationale: Heavy-lift drones and later crawler robots that work on blades at height outdoors needed hardware, control and safety engineering beyond a small software team.

defensibility.rationale: Patented robots and accumulated field operations with OEMs and operators, but rope access crews and other robot makers offer substitutes.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found in sources; OEMs such as GE and Siemens Gamesa appear as customers.

market_need_then: Blade maintenance relied on dangerous rope work. Aerones named wind power as the market after early rescue and firefighting drone ideas proved too small and hard to regulate, per a search summary of company history.

identity.visual_style: Industrial and technical, service-company site with customer portal

branding.community_and_virality: No evidence of community or merch found; press covers funding and technology rather than the brand.

brand_strength.rationale: Brand searches returned funding coverage and a TIME greentech mention in company news but nothing about name, mascot or community.

pivots.from: Heavy-lift drones for rescue and firefighting
pivots.to: Drones and robots for wind turbine maintenance
pivots.why: Early markets were small and urban drone rules were a barrier (search summary of company history, not fully verified)

outcome_analysis: Aerones moved from heavy-lift drones into robot-enabled wind turbine maintenance, then shifted to ground-based robots in 2020. It sold services to large operators and OEMs and raised a seed in 2022, a Series A in 2023 and a 62 million dollar round in 2025. No acquisition, layoff or shutdown reports were found, and its site claims a large share of global wind capacity as customers.
notes: Dealroom lists a December 2022 Series A at 38.9 million dollars, unverified and conflicting with 30 million in January 2023. Tech.eu cites about 41 million total at Series A. The 2025 round is labeled Series B by Dealroom and seed by Seedtable, so stage is other. One search summary names Andris Dambis as a third co-founder, but the YC page and company about page list only two, so he is not recorded. Founding year 2015 per YC page. Rope Robotics source is dated about nine months after the batch.
